gaps.gap: The Action Gateway modal supports ONLY a single ActionRequest, not a bundled multi-step ActionPlan with step-by-step approval. The modal renders a flat 'What will happen' consequence list (item.conseq), never a step list. Every gateway item in data (q1/q2/edit/perm) is a single action; openGateway(id) selects exactly one. There is no submit_action_plan path, no per-step rows, no step status, no per-step risk/preview/rollback. This directly violates owner decision O-3 (full multi-step bundled ActionPlan + step-by-step approval is MVP-blocking).
gaps.kit_evidence: kit-overlays.jsx GatewayModal lines 38-74 (renders item.conseq, no steps); kit-data.js gateway.{q1,q2,edit,perm} are single ActionRequests; index.html lines 100-105 openGateway picks one item id

gaps.recommendation: Change the kit: the Gateway modal MUST render the Screen-16 layout (Action summary / Risk banner / Step list / Preview-per-step / Affected resources / Evidence / Permissions / Approval controls / Audit note) backed by an ActionPlan{steps[], dependencies, overallRisk, approvalMode} data shape, not a single conseq array.
gaps.for_tasks_gen: Gateway Review Modal must accept an ActionPlan (1..N ActionPlanSteps) and render a step list; each step row shows step number, action type, target, risk level, preconditions, preview/dry-run status, rollback availability, and step status. A single ActionRequest is the N=1 degenerate case of the same component. Bind to ARCH §6.2 + Appendix A ActionPlan/ActionPlanStep.

gaps.gap: Step-by-step approval controls are entirely absent from the Gateway modal. UX Screen 16 mandates seven controls (Approve all, Approve step-by-step, Deny, Edit plan, Remove step, Require manual execution, Save as policy if eligible). The prototype offers only Deny + Approve-once (two buttons) plus an 'Always allow' checkbox. Missing: approve-all-eligible, approve-individual-step, edit-step-before-approve, remove-step, require-manual-execution, save-as-policy, deny-with-reason.
gaps.kit_evidence: kit-overlays.jsx GatewayModal footer lines 64-70 (only Deny + Approve once + 'Always allow' checkbox); no edit/remove/manual/save-as-policy/per-step controls

gaps.recommendation: Change the kit: add the full Screen-16 control set; wire step_id into the approve action and surface PolicyDecision.require_step_approval. Map 'Save as policy' to approvalScope='policy_grant' (AG §9.5) and 'Always allow' to the same grant flow.
gaps.for_tasks_gen: Gateway modal controls must implement: approve-all-eligible (excludes critical by default), approve-individual-step (step_id), edit-before-approve (re-preview + re-risk, never execute an unapproved diff per ARCH §6.2 stale-precondition rule), remove-step, require-manual-execution, deny-with-reason (deny carries reason -> ARCH §6.1 deny(approval_id, reason)), and save-as-policy when eligible (approvalScope policy_grant). Critical (risk 4) actions must never appear in approve-all by default.

This breaks the Ask-Brain->multi-step-ActionPlan->step-approve flow (ARCH §8 'Ask Brain + action plan' / PRD §9.11-12 / O-3) and the propose->preview->step-approve seam.

gaps.gap: The Brain drawer header omits required provenance/transport/index-status indicators. UX Screen 14 header fields = Scope, Index status, Evidence mode, Action mode, Privacy/transport indicator. The kit shows a static 'grounded · 142 objects' badge and a 'co-pilot' badge only — no live ProjectBrain status (the 10-state machine: indexing/stale/partial_index/degraded/reindex_required/error), no privacy/transport (stdio MCP vs loopback-HTTP fallback) indicator, no evidence-mode/action-mode toggles.
